correctness.rationale: Uniform argument: all n>=19 have precisely n simple hexagons; all graph-square cliques consist of centered neighborhood tetrahedra plus exactly two maximal triangles per hexagon (radius-two ball intersections prove maximality); 8n explicit free-face pairs collapse the centered subcomplex onto GP(n,3); the 2n missing faces become paired disks on the n hexagon loops. Removing one disk/unique inner edge per loop retracts the first-disk complex to the outer circle, while second disks yield n spheres. Each octahedral sphere z_i is an integral basis vector in the cellular model. Reflection on the join orientation changes two signs and preserves z_i; rotation permutes. This proves the all-n homotopy and integral dihedral modules. The independent finite checker builds 54 sizes n=19..72, reproduces collapses and oriented cycles for eight, computes binary boundary ranks for nine, and exactly verifies the n=18 obstruction. No finite bound is treated as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Direct published-claim implications were tested rather than titles. The closest 2011 paper excludes girth six or requires all graph-square cliques to be centered; the two published all-graph hexagon theorems exclude shared hexagon edges; the generalized Petersen result is for inner step two. The uniform inner-step-three homotopy, primitive basis, and integral dihedral action were not implied by these sources or returned indexed claims. This is best-knowledge originality, not a uniqueness certificate.

value.rationale: The theorem fills a structural all-n gap for a classical cubic graph family whose dense overlapping six-cycles invalidate known edge-disjoint hexagon results. It produces a natural homotopy transition with primitive integral persistence kernel, canonical two-sphere generators and exact integral dihedral permutation action. The n=18 obstruction establishes a meaningful stable-range boundary; these features are not mere recomputation of a known numerical table or an arbitrary slice.
